title: ST558 Homework 2
text:
Task 1: Basic Vector practice
Suppose we have data from a medical experiment on blood pressure. We have the following pre-treatment values for subjects 1 through 20:
• 130, 128, 116, 124, 133, 134, 118, 126, 114, 127, 141, 138, 128, 140, 137, 131, 120, 128, 139, 135
after treatment, the subjects were measured again (subjects 1 through 20 match)
• 114, 98, 113, 99, 107, 116, 113, 111, 119, 117, 101, 119, 130, 122, 106, 106, 124, 102, 117, 113
1) Create two vectors. One vector corresponding to the pre measurements and one to the post measurements.
Solution:

# Pre-treatment blood pressure measurements
pre_bp <- c(
  130, 128, 116, 124, 133,
  134, 118, 126, 114, 127,
  141, 138, 128, 140, 137,
  131, 120, 128, 139, 135
)

# Post-treatment blood pressure measurements
post_bp <- c(
  114, 98, 113, 99, 107,
  116, 113, 111, 119, 117,
  101, 119, 130, 122, 106,
  106, 124, 102, 117, 113
)

pre_bp

 [1] 130 128 116 124 133 134 118 126 114 127 141 138 128 140 137 131 120 128 139
[20] 135

post_bp

 [1] 114  98 113  99 107 116 113 111 119 117 101 119 130 122 106 106 124 102 117
[20] 113


Above I created one vector for the pre-treatment measurements and another vector for the post-treatment measurements.
2) Assign names to the vector elements using the paste() function. Note that names() can be overwritten by a character vector. To quickly create the names, try running the code paste. Create the same names for each vector’s elements
Solution:

subject_names <- paste("Subject", 1:20, sep = "_")

names(pre_bp) <- subject_names
names(post_bp) <- subject_names

Subject_15 Subject_16 Subject_17 Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20

3) Calculate the change in blood pressure for each patient by subtracting post-treatment measurements from pre-treatment measurements. Recall that R does math element-wise! Save this calculation as a new object (also a vector).
Solution:

# Calculate the change in blood pressure
change_bp <- pre_bp - post_bp

change_bp

Subject_15 Subject_16 Subject_17 Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20

A positive value means that the blood pressure decreased after treatment.
4) Calculate the average decrease in blood pressure across all patients.
Solution:
I used the mean() function to calculate the average change across all 20 subjects.

# Calculate the average change for all subjects
mean(change_bp)

[1] 17


From the result above we note that the average change is 17 mmHg.
5) Determine which patients experienced a decrease in blood pressure after treatment (a positive change). Use the which() function to just return the indices (and names) associated with this type of change.
Solution:
A positive change means that the pre-treatment blood pressure was greater than the post-treatment blood pressure. I used the which() to find the positions where the change is greater than zero.
